standard.title: Arts importance for communities
standard.description: explore how and why the arts are important for people and communities
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have personal experience of arts events (songs at celebrations, animations, dances) but have not yet consciously reflected on why the arts matter to communities or what role they play.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify arts works and experiences from their lives and explain how they are important for people and communities.

nodes.label: Arts in my life
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify at least two types of arts works or experiences from their own life or community (e.g. a song, a dance, a cartoon, a game, public art).
nodes.minimum_width: Name and briefly describe two arts experiences from their own life — school-based and community-based (e.g. birthday songs and a TV animation).
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe a range of arts works and experiences encountered at school, home and in the community — songs, dances, animations, computer games, public art, performances; share ideas and feelings about these works with peers and teachers.
wider: Identify arts works encountered in digital and screen contexts (computer games, music videos, animations) and compare how these feel different from live performances or physical artworks
Listen to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of arts for connecting to people, culture and Country/Place — using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot identify arts works in their own lives, they have no concrete examples to connect to the 'why arts matter' question — subsequent discussion of community importance has no grounding.

response_modes.reason: Ensure students encounter arts examples from multiple contexts — digital/screen, live performance, community celebration, cultural ceremony — so their repertoire of 'what counts as arts' is broad enough to ground later exploration.

success_criteria: Student can name at least two different arts works or experiences from their own life
Student can describe where or when they encounter each one

nodes.label: How arts communicate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how arts works communicate feelings, ideas or cultural knowledge — using examples they have encountered.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one way an arts work communicates something — e.g. how a character's face shows an emotion, how a song makes them feel, how images in a book tell a story.
nodes.typical_width: Explore how facial expressions, gestures, movement, voice and language communicate emotions in arts works; describe how illustrations in books communicate character, setting and mood; identify how songs used at celebrations communicate shared meaning or purpose.
wider: Explore how illustrations and images in picture books or screen texts communicate narrative, character and mood — connecting arts exploration to literacy and building vocabulary for describing how arts communicate
Compare how a favourite song used at a celebration (birthday, sports, school event) communicates differently to the same song heard without context — discussing what the occasion adds to the meaning

response_modes.reason: Students benefit from explicit scaffolding to move from 'this makes me feel...' to 'this communicates... because...'. Structured questioning (What does this face tell you? How does the music change?) builds the reasoning habit.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of communicative modes available in Foundation arts (gesture, facial expression, voice, image, music) is genuinely rich for exploration — students who investigate across modes develop a much stronger vocabulary for arts analysis.
success_criteria: Student can identify what an arts work is communicating (a feeling, a story, a message)
Student can describe at least one feature of the work that communicates this (a sound, an image, a gesture)

nodes.label: Why arts matter to communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why an arts work matters to a group of people — connecting the work to its community purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain one reason why a specific arts work matters to a community (e.g. 'We sing the birthday song because it makes everyone feel special on their birthday').
nodes.typical_width: Discuss why different arts works are important to different groups — school songs, cultural dances, animations that teach content; identify how arts works connect people and share cultural knowledge; engage with examples of First Nations Australians explaining the importance of arts for culture and Country.
wider: Listen to and discuss stories shared by First Nations Australians about the importance of arts for connecting to people, culture and Country/Place — and compare this to how arts works matter in students' own communities
Identify social or cultural dances that have meaning for people and communities (taking care to observe protocols) — exploring why these dances are performed and what is lost if they are not

response_modes.reason: This node integrates identification of arts works with understanding of their community function — connect students' concrete examples from Node 1 to the 'why it matters' question.

success_criteria: Student can explain why a specific arts work matters to a group of people
Student can connect an arts work to its community or cultural purpose
